name: Hipódromo de la Zarzuela

position.source: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/24542681 (centroid of the row of grandstands; its long side faces 87.7°, the track)

rights.note: Grandstands by the architects Carlos Arniches and Martín Domínguez with the engineer Eduardo Torroja, who designed the shell roofs; built 1935–1936, finished after the Civil War and opened in 1941; rehabilitated 2004–2016. Bien de Interés Cultural (Real Decreto 1611/2009). Martín Domínguez died in 1970; authors who died before 1987 keep 80 years of protection in Spain, so the work is protected until the end of 2050 (public domain from 2051).

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q1620086_hipodromo_de_la_zarzuela.py, tools/meshkit.py) with AI assistance. The three grandstands of the racecourse, facing the track (+Z, east). Each roof is a row of 5 m modules (12, 6 and 12, sizes and positions from the PNOA orthophoto), each module a thin shell vaulting upwards between two frames, so the edges are rows of arches; in section a V: the 12.8 m cantilever over the terraces rising to ≈ 13.6 m at the front edge, a rear arm rising to ≈ 12.6 m over the upper gallery, one column under the low point (≈ 11 m) on every frame and a steel tie behind it; the shell is 65 cm thick at the column and 6 cm at the edges (the vaults are simplified to parabolic arches, rise 0.55 m at the column to 1.3 m at the edges; the true hyperboloid geometry is not reproduced exactly). Under each roof: 16 concrete terraces (the first rows with green seats) up to 7.5 m, the upper gallery with glazed booths, the base building with one arch per module on its back (paddock) wall, and round stair towers at both ends. Low white blocks fill the OSM building between the grandstands and at its south end (bars and passages, simplified). The white rail in front is the near rail of the turf course (from the orthophoto); the course, the pelouse and the paddock are left to the map. Heights from photos (±1 m). The central grandstand is set back about 4 m from the other two, as in the orthophoto. Not modelled: the paddock galleries, restaurants and other buildings of the complex, signs and furniture.
